title: An aven-brand skill
description:
A skill is a DOCUMENT, not a file of prose — the same decision the unit library made. `units/*.json` declares what a component is and the engine renders it; `skills/*.json` declares what a skill is and the generator writes it. The reason is identical in both places: a document can be validated at load, and a skill that names a gate which does not exist, or a depth file that was deleted, should fail when the library is built rather than when someone invokes it and gets a dead reference.

What this buys that 41 loose SKILL.md files did not: every skill is guaranteed to route somewhere real, no two skills can claim the same trigger, and the consumable form is generated rather than hand-maintained — so the frontmatter cannot drift from the body.

name.description: The invocation name. `/design-component` runs the skill named `design-component`.

summary.description: One line. It becomes the description Claude Code matches against, so it says what the skill DOES, not what it is about.

area.description: Which half of the lifecycle. `foundation` is tokens and brand; `build` makes something; `verify` checks it; `operate` keeps a used system healthy; `communicate` explains it to people who are not in it. The ops half — operate and communicate — is what the UI/UX kit had almost nothing of.

trigger.description: When to reach for this and when not to. The `not` half is load-bearing: two skills that both sound right for a request is the most common failure of a large library, and the only cure is for each to say what it is NOT.

instead.description: Map of situation -> the skill that actually handles it. Validated: every value must name a real skill.

reads.description: Depth files this skill loads, relative to the repo root. Validated to exist — a skill pointing at a deleted rule file is a skill that silently does less.

gates.description: Runnable gates, by FILENAME in skills/gates. Validated to exist. A skill with no gates has to say why in `done`, because 'looks right' is not a verification.

output.description: The shape of what the skill produces.

done.description: Definition of done, in terms a reader can check. Not 'the component is good' — 'the gate printed N/N'.

supersedes.description: Skills from a merged library that this one absorbed, so the merge is a record rather than a deletion.
